numberingDecision: The TC-10.1–TC-10.8 references in KAN-89 are canonical. Jira child summaries retain their historical suffixes, but this ledger fixes the editorial order independently.

entries.title: The Shape of a Civilization
entries.interactivePattern: Comparative timeline that shifts attention from bounded territory to roads, rivers, settlements and ecological systems
entries.roomRationale: The essay anchors The Earth by treating civilisation as a changing relation between settlement and ground rather than as a coloured territorial silhouette.

entries.title: The Cartography of Empire
entries.interactivePattern: Administrative-sheet sequence comparing Sanson and Zatta classifications, borders and inherited geographic plates
entries.roomRationale: The Border is primary because the essay reads administrative divisions as active instruments of imperial legibility, with archives and cities exposing their production.

entries.title: When Maps Create Countries
entries.interactivePattern: Claim sequence separating survey, repetition, schooling and administration in the production of national territory
entries.roomRationale: The essay belongs to The Border because it asks how repeated mapped lines become institutions and identities, not merely how states are illustrated after formation.

entries.title: Projection and Perspective
entries.interactivePattern: Projection-choice sequence exposing which spatial relationships each mathematical surface preserves and sacrifices
entries.roomRationale: The Map is primary because projection is examined as a formal choice that turns a situated view of the Earth into a repeatable graphic argument.

entries.title: The Geography of Power
entries.interactivePattern: Layered civic-service map contrasting jurisdiction, infrastructure and lived access
entries.roomRationale: The City is primary because the essay locates power in everyday spatial systems—parcels, services, policing and access—rather than only at a national border.

entries.title: Invisible Maps of Migration
entries.interactivePattern: Uncertainty-aware flow sequence that distinguishes recorded journeys from the administrative traces left behind
entries.roomRationale: The Road is primary because movement and interrupted movement organise the essay, while borders and archives explain why some journeys become visible and others disappear.

entries.title: Palimpsest Landscapes
entries.interactivePattern: Layer-stripping comparison across survey, demolition, reuse and archaeological reconstruction
entries.roomRationale: The Archive is primary because the landscape is read as an accumulation of surviving, erased and reinterpreted records embedded in earth and settlement.

entries.title: Classification Is Cartography
entries.interactivePattern: Adjustable classification matrix showing how category boundaries reorganise the same collection of mapped objects
entries.roomRationale: The Theatre is primary because classification is treated as a staging of knowledge that arranges what can be compared, retrieved and left outside the frame.
